Low-Poly Asset Study: Tilápia Fish (PlayStation 1 Hardware Rendering)

Technical reconstruction of a cigarette pack using authentic PlayStation 1 rendering constraints:

・ Modeling: Polygons with vertex snapping

・ Texturing: hand-painted texture + affine warping artifacts

・ Shading: Software-style dithering + vertex lighting (no modern PBR)

・ Intentional limitations: No smoothing, subpixel precision, or mipmapping.


Created as a reference for retro game asset pipelines and 3D art preservation. Explores how technical hardware flaws (affine UV interpolation, fixed-point arithmetic) defined the PS1’s distinctive visual language.

name: Green Tortoise Beetle (Cassida viridis)
description:
Scan of Green tortoise beetle (*Cassida viridis*) performed with Nikon XTH250 MicroCT at the [Microscopy Platform at Department of Biology](https://portal.research.lu.se/en/equipments/microscopy-platform-at-department-of-biology), Lund University, with support from [InfraVis](https://infravis.se/), the Swedish National Infrastructure for Data Visualization. Involved people: Filip Berendt, Ingemar Markström.

**Phenotyping the morphology of the green tortoise beetle *Cassida viridis* in order to understand evolution**

In this project, we investigate divergence, local adaptation and how the rate of microevolution is affected by environmental factors in wild populations of the green tortoise beetle. The 3D-scan enable us to measure various morphological traits. By estimating the phenotypic variation and covariation between traits, we can investigate how and why populations differ in their ability to adapt to environmental changes.

Project by [ Maja Tarka](https://portal.research.lu.se/en/persons/maja-tarka).
